      - name: week

      - name: month
        data_type: DATE

      - name: page_recency_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Row number per page_id ordered by created_timestamp descending; 1 is most recent; ties are ordered arbitrarily
      - name: rolling_7_post_shares
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Sum of shares over the current and six prior posts per page_id ordered by created_timestamp; includes the current row; shares default to 0
      - name: engagement_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: If impressions are 0 then 0.0; otherwise (likes + shares + comments) divided by impressions; computed as a double and not capped

      source_models:
      - staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organic_tweets
      business_logic: '- Input: include only records where organic_tweet_id is present. - Grouping: aggregate by organic_tweet_id and account_id to form post-level groups. - created_timestamp: earliest date in the group; null if all dates are missing. - post_message: the lexicographically last non-null tweet_text in the group; if all are missing, result is null; original casing and whitespace are preserved. - page_name: for each row, choose the first non-blank among screen_name, user_name, then account_id as text (blank strings treated as missing); from these per-row candidates, select the lexicographically last value in the group; may be null; original casing and whitespace are preserved. - platform: set to the literal value twitter. - Metrics aggregation: clicks, impressions, likes, retweets, replies, app_clicks, url_clicks, and qualified_impressions are summed per group, ignoring missing values. If a metric has no values in a group, it remains null at this stage. - Renames: shares is the sum of retweets; comments is the sum of replies. - engagement_rate: average of engagement_rate within the group, ignoring missing values; remains null if no values exist. - Final outputs: - page_id is account_id. - post_id is the text form of organic_tweet_id. - clicks, impressions, likes, shares, comments, app_clicks, url_clicks, and qualified_impressions default to 0 when null. - engagement_rate defaults to 0.0 when null. - post_url is built as https://twitter.com/{page_name}/status/{post_id}; if page_name is null, post_url is null; no URL encoding; casing preserved. - calculated_engagement_rate: if impressions (after defaulting) is greater than 0, compute (likes + shares + comments) divided by impressions using the zero-defaulted values; otherwise return 0.0; result is floating point. - Output: one row per (account_id, organic_tweet_id).'

      description: Monthly CTR and engagement metrics by platform and normalized content type with post and active account counts

      - intermediate.social_media_reporting__instagram_posts_reporting
      - intermediate.social_media_reporting__linkedin_posts_reporting

      - intermediate.social_media_reporting__youtube_videos_reporting
      business_logic: '- Union all posts from the five intermediate reporting models and assign a platform label: facebook, instagram, linkedin, twitter, youtube. - Derive content_type per source: - Facebook: if content_type is null, use "text". - Instagram: if content_format is null, use "feed post". - LinkedIn: if post_category is null, use "text post". - Twitter: classify the lowercased post_message: if it contains an http(s):// URL → "link"; else if it mentions "image" or "photo" → "photo"; else if it mentions "video" → "video"; otherwise "text". - YouTube: always "video". - Normalize each row: - month = created_timestamp truncated to the calendar month (first day). - content_type is lowercased. - clicks, impressions, likes, shares, comments: treat null as 0. - Aggregate by platform, month, content_type: - posts_count: number of rows (union-all, no de-duplication). - active_accounts_count: distinct count of page_id. - clicks, impressions, likes, shares, comments: sum of normalized values. - Compute rates from aggregated totals: - ctr: clicks divided by impressions when impressions > 0 and at least one active account; otherwise 0.0. - engagement_rate: (likes + shares + comments) divided by impressions when impressions > 0; otherwise 0.0. - Output one row per (platform, month, content_type); rates are DOUBLE with no rounding or capping.'

- name: social_media_reporting__daily_kpis
      description: Daily KPIs by platform and content type with lowercase content_type, platform-specific date spine (DuckDB range, end-exclusive), zero-filling, and CTR/engagement rate calculations
      grain: One row per (platform, day, content_type); if no activity on a day, a single 'text' content_type row per platform is produced
      source_models:
      - intermediate.social_media_reporting__facebook_posts_reporting
      - intermediate.social_media_reporting__instagram_posts_reporting
      - intermediate.social_media_reporting__linkedin_posts_reporting
      - intermediate.social_media_reporting__twitter_posts_reporting
      - intermediate.social_media_reporting__youtube_videos_reporting
      business_logic: '- Ingest five intermediate reporting models and assign platform: - facebook: content type defaults to "text" when missing. - instagram: content type defaults to "Feed Post" when missing. - linkedin: content type defaults to "Text Post" when missing. - twitter: derive content type from the post message (lowercased): contains a URL → "link"; contains "image" or "photo" → "photo"; contains "video" → "video"; otherwise "text". - youtube: content type is "video". - Normalize rows: - day is the calendar day derived from created_timestamp. - content_type is lowercased; no de-duplication. - Aggregate by (platform, day, content_type): - posts_count: number of posts. - active_accounts_count: distinct count of page_id. - clicks, impressions, likes, shares, comments: sums with nulls treated as zero. - Build a platform-specific date spine: - For each platform, find the earliest and latest day in normalized data. - Generate a daily series from the earliest day up to (but excluding) the latest boundary day using DuckDB''s date range generator. - Left join aggregates to the spine on (platform, day): - If no aggregates exist for a day, emit one row with content_type "text" and all metrics set to 0. - If aggregates exist, emit one row per content_type with the aggregated metrics. - Compute rates: - ctr: clicks divided by impressions when impressions > 0 and active_accounts_count > 0; otherwise 0.0. - engagement_rate: (clicks + likes + shares + comments) divided by impressions when impressions > 0; otherwise 0.0. - Outputs are non-null; counts and sums preserve source duplicates; only active_accounts_count uses a distinct page_id.'
      columns:
      - name: platform
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Platform label: facebook, instagram, linkedin, twitter, or youtube'
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: day
        data_type: DATE
        description: Calendar day derived from created_timestamp or the platform-specific spine; the spine starts at the earliest day and excludes the upper boundary day
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: content_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Lowercased normalized content type; defaults to 'text' on spine-only days; twitter from message patterns, instagram from content_format (default 'Feed Post'), linkedin from post_category (default 'Text Post'), youtube 'video'
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: posts_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of posts per (platform, day, content_type); duplicates preserved; zero on spine-only days
      - name: active_accounts_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of page_id per (platform, day, content_type); zero on spine-only days; used to guard the CTR denominator
      - name: clicks
        data_type: HUGEINT

- name: social_media_reporting__retention_kpis
      description: Weekly retention KPIs by platform using posting-activity cohorts over a fixed 13-week window
      grain: One row per platform per cohort_week per week_offset
      source_models:
      - intermediate.social_media_reporting__facebook_posts_reporting
      - intermediate.social_media_reporting__instagram_posts_reporting
      - intermediate.social_media_reporting__linkedin_posts_reporting
      - intermediate.social_media_reporting__twitter_posts_reporting
      - intermediate.social_media_reporting__youtube_videos_reporting
      business_logic: '- Inputs: - Union page activity from the five source models; only keep rows where created_timestamp is present. - Assign platform as one of: "facebook", "instagram", "linkedin", "twitter", "youtube". - Weekly normalization: - Bucket activity into ISO weeks starting Monday 00:00. - A page is considered active in a week if it posts at least once; multiple posts in the same week do not increase the activity count. - Cohorts: - For each (page_id, platform), set cohort_week to the earliest week with activity. - For each (platform, cohort_week), cohort_pages is the number of unique pages in that cohort. - Observation spine: - Generate week_offset values from 0 to 12 inclusive. - For each cohort, create 13 rows and set target_week to the start of the week that is week_offset weeks after cohort_week; when week_offset = 0, target_week equals cohort_week. - Activity presence: - Build distinct (platform, week, page_id) combinations so each active page-week is counted once. - Retention: - For each spine row, retained_pages is the number of unique pages active on the platform in target_week; this is not limited to members of the cohort. - KPI: - retention_rate = retained_pages divided by cohort_pages when cohort_pages > 0; otherwise 0.0. - No rounding; stored as double precision; values may exceed 1.0 due to the numerator scope. - Output: - Emit platform, cohort_week, week_offset, target_week, cohort_pages, retained_pages, retention_rate. - No explicit ordering is applied.'
      columns:
      - name: platform
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Platform name in lowercase: facebook, instagram, linkedin, twitter, or youtube'
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: cohort_week
        data_type: DATE
        description: Start date (Monday) of the first week the page is active for the platform
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: week_offset
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of weeks since cohort_week, inclusive 0 to 12
        tests:
        - not_null
        - week_offset BETWEEN 0 AND 12
      - name: target_week
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Start-of-week timestamp at week_offset weeks after cohort_week; equals cohort_week when offset is 0
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: cohort_pages
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique pages in the cohort for each (platform, cohort_week)
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: retained_pages
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique pages active on the platform in target_week; one count per page-week; not limited to cohort members
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: retention_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE

        - retention_rate >= 0
